text:
maria: Quick question — for Console telemetry + rollout UX, should our internal APIs be gRPC-first (protobufs + streaming) or JSON/REST-first? Thinking about browser compatibility, quotas, routing/fallbacks and rollout ergonomics. Opinions?

alex: gRPC-first for service->service. Streaming + typed protos give way less brittle telemetry and make canarying by method/version easier. For browser clients we can expose a thin HTTP gateway.

devon: Agree on backend gRPC, but the gateway is non-trivial — where do we enforce quotas and routing? At the gateway we can short-circuit bad clients, but we lose smart routing context if runtime needs tenant signals.

lina: If gateway enforces quotas we should pass a signed tenant claim header so runtime can still make routing decisions. Also we need consistent quota metrics in the Console.

nate: FWIW the Envoy ext_auth + grpc-transcoding spike I ran showed a 10-15% CPU tax on heavy transcoding routes. Telemetry also lost a few spans because headers were mutated.

sam: Can we see the spike notes? Also from a UX POV rollouts want per-route/model canaries. Protos make versioning explicit; JSON diffs get messy fast.

maria: Nate — can you paste the spike log snippet here? Need concrete numbers to weigh operational cost vs dev ergonomics. Also proposal: provide a documented JSON fallback endpoint that hits an HTTP bridge which transcodes to gRPC for browsers that can't do bidi streams.

nate: sure, here's the snippet I used to repro the transcoding pain: 
```bash
# quick repro: send a streaming request through the gateway
curl -v -H "Content-Type: application/grpc" --data-binary @payload.bin https://gateway.prod.internal/edge/stream
```
Logs showed repeated 502s when payloads hit the transcoder under CPU pressure.

deploy-bot: gateway-canary v2 rolled to prod-edge-3 :rocket: — no critical errors in the last 10m.

alex: Proposal: backend = proto/gRPC-first; client-facing = explicit REST shim with clear SLOs (higher latency allowed). Add a header on all requests `x-internal-protocol: grpc|rest` and tag spans so Console can compare metrics by protocol.

lina: :thumbsup: Also add per-route metric for transcoding CPU ms and transcoding error rate. That will let us quantify cost for each route.

devon: Sounds good. Next action: RFC that codifies decision + migration plan and states where quotas are enforced (gateway vs runtime) with fallbacks. I'll draft.

maria: Perfect. Nate/Alex/Devon — can you each add a 2-paragraph section to the RFC about fallback routing, quota enforcement location, and telemetry tagging by EOW? Thanks!
